title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 3)
summary: NH reads and comments on book three of Marcus Aurelius' Meditations. He draws lessons on self-reliance and free thinking, rejecting immediate pleasure for the pleasure of self-mastery, freedom from others' judgment, owning the present, observing everything to keep getting smarter, staying pure through single-minded focus, and ignoring crabs in the bucket.
claims: A free thinker can explain his own train of thought; repeating what a person or book told you is not free thinking
Fear of rejection is a deep tribal instinct, but today the real consequences of standing alone are far smaller than for our ancestors
If a belief needs to silence or ignore others, it is not sound; a training method that only works in a vacuum and wobbles under comparison is a bad method
Stoicism rejects pleasures of passion: instant gratification like food or acts you'll regret; the payoff is the later pleasure of self-mastery
People are most productive alone; team work mainly forces the least productive members to do something
In big companies roughly 20% of the workforce does 95% of the work
Even alone you are not free if you are tortured by imagined judgment; much of what torments you is self-made
Everyone is born with the voice of reason; irrational people have stopped matching their reality to it
Keep your opinions consistent with each other, but never let a group dictate a package of beliefs you must adopt
Only the present is controllable; don't lament the past, and the future becomes the present you control
Examine everything, even things you find uninteresting; observation is how intelligence keeps growing with age
Like muscularity, intelligence keeps improving with time; if you think you were as smart 10 years ago, you stopped progressing
Purity is going straight from A to B; corruption creeps in through extra steps, so pursue goals with single-minded focus
The only thing that stops people is fear of what others will think; drop it and no one can hinder you
People trying to rise attract crabs in the bucket who want them mediocre; ignore them
You can't change people by telling them what to do; lead by example and live your life
